verdicts.why: Names an outcome without judging it; the plain word for what follows from something.
A solution-statement in the technical sense; describes without taking a side.
A grammatical term for a semantic role; carries no attitude at all.
To make something more temperate by admixture is a plain process verb, not a judgement of it.
To moderate or restrain; describes the change, says nothing about whether the speaker approves.
Metallurgical hardening; a technical process with no stance.
Bringing a material to a consistency by heating and cooling; purely technical.
Tuning a piano's pitch; a craft term without judgement.
Emotional disturbance is an unpleasant referent, but the word reports the state plainly rather than sneering at or pitying it.
Physically set in motion, as of liquid or air; a neutral description.
A small thicket of bushes; a plain landscape noun like 'field' or 'hedge'.
An intensifier meaning beyond doubt; it strengthens the claim but adds no attitude toward its object.
To try to prevent or oppose is a plain description of an act, with no view on whether the act is right.
Depriving of hope is a bad thing to do, but the verb names the effect plainly; the referent is bad, not the word.
Advising against a course of behaviour; neutral counsel verb.
To give a right to is the plain legal-moral verb; the sneering 'entitled' of modern usage is a separate adjective sense not printed here.
To give a title to a book or work; purely descriptive.
To ennoble someone; a formal act named without attitude.
Great volume is the meaning, not an attitude; 'loud' is itself the plain neighbour that words like 'blaring' or 'raucous' are loaded against.
A musical performance direction; technical and unjudging.
The favourable outcome is part of the meaning; the word takes no stance beyond naming the good fortune.
Chance as the cause of one outcome over another; neutral, and can be good or bad.
One's overall lot in life; a plain noun for circumstances.
The good-fortune evaluation is the word's meaning rather than an attitude carried beyond it, so a learner needs no warning about how it lands.
An anatomical bundle of fibres; wholly neutral.
Courage to carry on is the meaning itself, like 'courage'; the impudence sense of 'nerve' is a different synset not printed here.
To accept an excuse; a plain, if formal, verb of forgiving.
To grant an official pardon; legal and unjudging.
A walkway laid for a purpose; a plain concrete noun.
A course of conduct, figuratively a road; names the course without judging it.
